draft.title: Social and emotional development
card: Learning to relate to other people, such as making friends, sharing, cooperating and working in a group.
Learning to understand and manage feelings, such as staying calm when upset or recognising how someone else feels.
Both change as people form new relationships, for example with carers, friends, teammates, partners or workmates.
The two areas are linked. A person who can manage anger may find it easier to keep friendships, and good friendships can help a person cope with stress.
draft.remember: Social is about relating to others. Emotional is about understanding and managing feelings. New relationships shape both.

opts: A child learns to take a breath when frustrated
A child learns to ride a bike without help
A child learns to read a short story aloud
A child grows 6 cm taller over one year
a.why: Managing a feeling such as frustration is emotional development. Riding a bike is physical, reading is intellectual, and growing taller is growth in size. Learning to share with friends would be social, but that is not an option here.
a.clue: Which one is about handling a feeling?

b.q: Jaya, 16, joins a netball team in Bendigo. Over the season she learns to cooperate with teammates and to cope with a loss without lashing out. What does this show?
opts: Social and emotional development, both shaped by a new group
Social development only, as a team is a group of people
Emotional development only, as losing is an upsetting event
Physical development, as netball is a sport
b.why: Cooperating with teammates is social development. Coping with a loss without lashing out is emotional development. The new team relationship shapes both. Saying social only is tempting because a team is a group, but the card links the two areas.
b.clue: Look for both a skill with people and a skill with feelings.

a.best: A child learns to take a breath when frustrated

b.best: Social and emotional development, both shaped by a new group

problems.detail: The clue 'Look for both a skill with people and a skill with feelings' points straight to the only option that says 'both', so a student can pick the answer without weighing the scenario.

check.summary: The card, the questions and the explanations are accurate and fit the point. The only issue is that question b's clue all but names the answer by telling students to look for 'both'.
